title: All, from the Sun's Uprise
description: All, from the Sun's Uprise in Tonic Solfa to DARWALL, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: George Sandys wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 495, “Praise Ye the Lord”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Hallelujah Metre (6.6.6.6.4.4.4.4), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DARWALL; any other Hallelujah Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: All, from the sun's up-rise Un-to his set-ting rays, Re-sound in ju-bi-lees The great Cre-a-tor's praise! Him serve a-lone; In tri-umph bring Your gifts, and sing Be-fore His throne!

lines: Man drew from man his birth;
And praise Him in His courts.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: George Sandys died in 1644.
credits: Words by George Sandys (1578–1644), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to DARWALL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
